title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reading.body:
This is a system used outside the conditions it was built for. Flock cameras read only the letters and numbers on a plate, and Kansas issues the same plate number across more than 100 designs, about half of them specialty plates. The camera's output is a number match, not an identification of a vehicle, and the stops followed from that match.

Catching this would require information the system does not use. Reading the plate background or design, or checking the plate type against the stolen entry, would separate the minivan from the pickup. A human check before a stop is the stated safeguard, and the reporting says officers may have no alternative when a stolen entry carries the wrong plate type. The department has discussed training Flock's AI to recognize plate backgrounds, and Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit plates rather than eliminating duplicated numbers.

What is not established is fault. The reporting is a single outlet's investigation, and it contains no finding that any officer or the camera vendor acted unlawfully.

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were pulled over twice because their Kansas KU Alumni license plate number, 7007, matched a stolen GMC pickup's temporary tag. In Colwich, Kansas, police stopped them after a Flock camera alert, but an officer knew their minivan and explained the duplicate. About a month later in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock alert led police to stop them, point guns at them, and handcuff Matthew. Kansas duplicates plate numbers across more than 100 designs, about half specialty, and Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate backgrounds.

Wichita police Capt. Casey Slaughter said Flock alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but if a wrong plate type was entered as stolen, officers may have no other choice. The department has discussed training Flock's AI to recognize plate backgrounds. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit, not duplicated plate numbers as the best fix. The Spurlocks' stolen plate entry has expired, so they no longer expect stops, and they hope to keep their 14 year old plate.
